summary.text: Democrat Garlin Gilchrist won the election for Michigan Secretary of State on November 3, 2026, defeating Anthony Forlini, according to unofficial results, and is set to take office when the new term begins.
A computer engineer by training, he has been lieutenant governor since 2019 and left the race for governor in January 2026 to run for secretary of state.

paragraphs.text: Gilchrist is a computer engineer by training; according to his official state biography he is a software engineer.
In 2017 he ran unsuccessfully for Detroit city clerk against incumbent Janice Winfrey.
He has been lieutenant governor since 2019, serving alongside Gov. Gretchen Whitmer.
In January 2026 Gilchrist dropped out of the race for governor and entered the Secretary of State race.
Michigan Democrats chose him as their nominee for secretary of state at the party's convention on April 19, 2026.
His state biography says he lives in Detroit with his wife and children.
During the campaign, he emphasized protecting voter data from federal access, campaign-finance transparency and better Secretary of State branch services.

He won the November 3, 2026 general election for Secretary of State of Michigan with 53.8% of the vote to Anthony Forlini's 43.5% and Christine Sloan's 1.6% and 2 other candidates, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
